title: T-014 verifies an orphan dataLayer; production fetch path is uncovered
description: T-014 (network-shape lockdown) drives `runDataLayer`, a self-contained 30-line function that issues `sui_getObject` and `suix_queryEvents` directly via `fetch`. But `runDataLayer` is never imported by `App.tsx`, `fillFetcher.ts`, or any production wiring — App accepts an injected `fetchPoolStats` whose real implementation does not exist anywhere in the cycle's src tree. The test thus locks down the URL shape of a function that ships dead, while the *actual* code path that will fetch chain data at runtime (whatever wires `fillFetcher.QueryEventsFn` to a Sui client and whatever satisfies `AppDeps.fetchPoolStats` in main.tsx) is unverified. The forbidden-URL guarantee that AC1.5 requires is not enforced against the code the user will run.
impact: AC1.5's no-indexer-pool-keyed-route invariant is only proven for an unused stub. The shipped SPA could call `:9008/get_pools` with no test catching it. The cycle's most important integration test is a tautology against an isolated fixture function.
recommendation: Either (a) wire `runDataLayer` into the App as the production fetch path so T-014 covers what users hit, or (b) add a parallel network-shape test that drives App with a real `fetchPoolStats` (the one that main.tsx actually constructs) under a fetch spy. The current setup green-lights AC1.5 without proving it.

title: T-019/T-020 pass because App echoes the stub's own error message verbatim
description:
T-019 stubs loadManifest to throw `'Deployment manifest not found at /tmp/missing.json. Run `pnpm deploy-all` from the deepbook-sandbox repo.'`, then asserts the rendered DOM contains `/deploy-all|deepbook-sandbox/i`. T-020 follows the same pattern with a stub error containing `127.0.0.1:9000` and regex matching it. App.tsx renders the raw error via `
{state.error}
` — so the assertion succeeds because the test's own stub message is dumped to the DOM, not because App constructed any 'actionable inline error UI'. If the contract's intent is that App provides the bootstrap recipe text itself, that intent is not tested; if the intent is that App surfaces the loader's error verbatim, the test is not adversarial enough — replace the stubbed error with `'whatever'` and the test would fail, proving it only checks string passthrough.
impact: AC1.1's 'actionable inline error UI' assertion is tautological. A future refactor that drops the error-rendering UI altogether would be caught, but a refactor that strips the bootstrap-recipe synthesis logic from the App (because there isn't any) would not. The contract requirement 'inline message naming the sandbox boot command' is unverified at the App layer; it is only verified inside the loader (T-003).
recommendation: Either explicitly assert the App contributes recipe text the loader did NOT provide (stub a generic 'EACCES' error and assert App still tells the user about deploy-all), OR rewrite the test name to honestly say 'App surfaces the loader's error message in an alert region' and drop the actionability framing.

title: PoolCard tests check labels but never assert sparkline values are rendered
description: T-015 checks six label patterns are present. The sparkline pattern is `/sparkline|trades/i`, satisfied by the label text alone (`Sparkline (last 50 trades)`). Neither T-015 nor T-016 asserts that the actual sparkline values from `data.sparkline` (e.g. `0.6700`, `0.6710`, `0.6720`) appear in the rendered output. A regression where PoolCard rendered the sparkline as an empty string or silently dropped it would pass both tests. Similarly, no test asserts that the numeric stat values (1234.56, 0.671, 0.6715, etc.) are visible — only that the labels are.
impact: AC1.3 requires the page to *display* six statistics; the tests only enforce that six labels exist. A bug where every value rendered as the sentinel placeholder `—` would pass T-015 against the populated fixture. The sparkline freshness story (E-001) leans on the sparkline actually rendering numbers, which no unit test checks.
recommendation: Add value assertions: e.g. `expect(screen.getByText('1234.56')).toBeInTheDocument()` for volume, and assert at least one sparkline tick value (`'0.6700'`) is rendered when `data.sparkline` is non-empty. The label-only check is fine in addition, but not as the sole gate.

title: No test exercises the 30-second sparkline refresh required by the contract
description: The contract Behavior section states 'the sparkline updates within thirty seconds whenever a new fill lands on chain' and the in-scope list calls out 'Periodic refresh of the fill stream so the sparkline reflects new fills within 30 s'. App.tsx's effect runs `loadManifest` + `fetchPoolStats` once on mount and never schedules a re-fetch. No test (unit or integration) drives a fake timer / second fetch and asserts a re-render. The contract accepts that E-001 covers part of this story but the per-cycle red/green loop never proves the refresh exists.
impact: A refresh bug (no setInterval, wrong interval, missed cleanup) ships green. AC1.3's freshness requirement has no executable test.
recommendation: Add an integration test using `vi.useFakeTimers()` that mounts App with a fetchPoolStats stub returning v1 data, advances time 30s, asserts fetchPoolStats is called again, and asserts the new card values appear. Alternatively, refactor refresh into a separate hook with its own unit test. Today the implementation has no refresh at all and no test would notice.

title: T-022 satisfied by any literal mention of 'chain-shape.md' regardless of derivation evidence
description: T-022 walks src/ and matches `/chain-shape\.md/i` against any file content. A doc comment containing only `// see chain-shape.md` satisfies it without proving any type was actually derived from a captured shape. The contract's intent (AC1.6: types derived from captured shapes) is not exercised — a developer could leave a misleading comment over a hand-guessed type and pass.
impact: AC1.6 traceability is structurally satisfied but not semantically. Low impact because AC1.6 is paired with G-PoolShape gating and end-of-cycle inspection.
recommendation: Either accept that T-022 is a sentinel marker test (and rename it to reflect that), or strengthen by requiring at least one `field-name`-level cross-reference between chain-shape.md and the type definitions (e.g. parse the markdown for backtick-quoted field names like `bids`, `asks`, `lot_size`, and assert each appears in src/types.ts or marketStats.ts).

title: T-013 third sub-test uses too-loose toBeGreaterThanOrEqual instead of toBe(50)
description: The 'first page already covers both stop conditions' sub-test asserts `expect(result.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(50)`. An implementation that fetched the first page (50 fills) and then continued through more pages would still pass this assertion as long as it eventually returned ≥50. The earlier sub-test (line 76) catches over-pagination via the call count, but this assertion specifically should pin the cap exactly with `.toBe(50)` to align with `MAX_FILLS = 50` and the contract's '50-fill cap'.
impact: Low: the sibling assertion `responder).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` already locks down pagination behavior. The looseness is purely on result-length specificity.
recommendation: Change to `expect(result.length).toBe(50)` for clarity. The current `>=50` would silently accept an off-by-one or duplicate-collection bug that produced 60 fills.

title: T-011 sparse sparkline: no assertion that values mirror input fills
description: T-011 asserts the sparkline length equals input length (3) and that each entry has finite numeric `price` and a `timestampMs` of type number. It never asserts the sparkline's prices/timestamps actually match the input fills (100, 101, 102). An implementation that returned `[{timestampMs: 0, price: 1}, {timestampMs: 0, price: 1}, {timestampMs: 0, price: 1}]` for any sparse input would pass.
impact: Sparse case behavior is undertested. The expressed intent ('consumer can render it without padding') is checked, but the implicit intent (the sparkline reflects the fills it was given) is not.
recommendation: Add `expect(result.sparkline.map(p => p.price)).toEqual([100, 101, 102])` and an analogous timestamp check. This costs one line and meaningfully strengthens the sparse-input behavior gate.

title: T-013 second sub-test does not assert in-window fills are returned
description: The 24h-window stop sub-test asserts (a) every returned fill is within 24h and (b) only two pages were queried. It does NOT assert the in-window fills count or content. An implementation that returned `[]` (collected nothing, then bailed) would trivially satisfy 'every f is within 24h' (vacuously) and the call count (it could still issue two queries). The vacuous-truth hole is small but real.
impact: An aggressive early-bail bug that stops after page 1 with empty `collected` would pass: forEach over [] doesn't fail the in-window predicate, and the responder would still get 1-2 calls depending on logic. Test does not pin a minimum result length.
recommendation: Add `expect(result.length).toBe(6)` (5 from page 1 + 1 from page 2 inside-window fill) so the predicate isn't vacuous.

title: T-018 console-error spy may miss async errors after waitFor resolves
description: T-018 mounts App, waits for one PoolCard to appear, then asserts `consoleErrSpy` was never called. React effects and async state transitions can log errors after the awaited assertion resolves; the test doesn't flush microtasks or wait for any 'fully settled' signal. A late console.error from an unhandled promise inside a fetchPoolStats branch could escape the spy window.
impact: AC1.1's 'no console errors during initial mount and paint' is checked at one specific moment, not across the full mount lifecycle. Mild — most React error logging is synchronous to the failing render.
recommendation: Either flush all pending promises before asserting (e.g. `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0))` after the waitFor), or document the test's window explicitly. Acceptable as-is for a smoke test.
